tuningIntent: Drop-tuned low string for weight; acoustic standard with open strings
referenceTraits: Mid-tempo 4/4 groove metal weight; the riff sits slightly behind the beat
Palm-muted low-register chug punctuated by open accents and hard silences
Snare backbeat placed late and heavy; kick answers the guitar instead of doubling it
Aggressive syncopation inside a straight pulse, never additive or metre-shifting
Blues-rooted minor lead with wide bends, hard vibrato and a real peak note
Clean acoustic close: dark modal colour, open strings ringing under moving inner voices
Northern melancholy in the acoustic passage; unhurried, no percussion, nothing damped
Space used as a rhythmic instrument; rests carry as much weight as hits

tracks.presetIntent: High-gain, tight low end with present midrange
tracks.tuningIntent: Drop-tuned low string for riff weight
tracks.energyJob: Holds the 4/4 floor and the riff weight; thins to sparse stabs under the solo
tracks.rationale: The piece's spine. It states the cell, tightens it in the break, moves it in the bridge, and then deliberately withdraws so the solo is heard over air rather than a wall.

tracks.presetIntent: High-gain lead voice with long sustain and bite
tracks.tuningIntent: Same drop tuning as the rhythm guitar
tracks.energyJob: Turns the riff cell into a singing line and carries the piece to its peak
tracks.rationale: Enters early in the bridge only as an accent double, so its full arrival in the solo is an event rather than a new instrument appearing from nowhere.

tracks.presetIntent: Natural steel-string acoustic, no drive, woody and open
tracks.tuningIntent: Standard tuning, open strings left ringing
tracks.energyJob: Carries the entire final third alone: dark, open-string, slow-moving
tracks.rationale: The closing passage is acoustic only. Its figure is the riff cell inverted and slowed, so the section reads as the same piece and not as an appended second piece.

tracks.presetIntent: Second clean acoustic voice, soft attack, upper register
tracks.tuningIntent: Standard tuning, matched to the acoustic guitar
tracks.energyJob: Adds a second acoustic line and interval colour, then withdraws before the end
tracks.rationale: A second acoustic voice, not an electric one: it supplies the suspended interval above the ringing tonic and leaves the last two bars to a single guitar.

tracks.presetIntent: Dry punchy kit, hard cracking snare, tight low tom
tracks.tuningIntent: Tight kick and tom tuning for articulation
tracks.energyJob: Changes groove role per section: plain pulse, syncopated answer, driving ride, fills
tracks.rationale: Presence comes from role changes rather than added hits: the kick converses with the guitar accents, the snare moves against them, and each section hands over with a differently shaped fill.

motifs.rhythmSignature: Two-bar cell: muted sixteenth cluster on beat 1, an empty 'and' of 2, hard hit landing just after beat 3
motifs.accentStructure: Beat 1 and the delayed beat-3 hit are accented; everything between stays muted and low
motifs.pitchContour: Root-anchored, leaning a semitone above the root and snapping back; total range under a fourth
motifs.spaceCharacter: The rest after beat 2 is the hook itself and must stay empty in every voice
motifs.rationale: A four-square cell with one displaced accent gives hard syncopation without disturbing the 4/4 pulse, so the break can be violent without sounding progressive or additive.

motifs.rhythmSignature: The same cell pushed an eighth later across each pair of bars, with the beat-3 hit doubled into a short pair
motifs.accentStructure: Accent migrates from beat 1 toward the 'and' of 3 while the kick keeps the true downbeat
motifs.pitchContour: Riff shape lifted a fourth, reaching up a minor sixth at the end of each phrase and not resolving
motifs.spaceCharacter: Holes shorten as the section closes, so the air runs out just before the solo
motifs.rationale: Development, not repetition: the same recognisable cell is displaced, lifted and compressed so the bridge is clearly derived from the break and still leaves stored tension for the solo.

motifs.rhythmSignature: One long held note, then a three-note group sequenced downward through the scale in even sixteenths
motifs.accentStructure: Attack on the held note, unaccented legato through the sequence, hard accent on the final bent target
motifs.pitchContour: Starts high, sequences down, then leaps back up a wide interval to a sustained bent peak
motifs.spaceCharacter: A full beat of silence after each phrase; the backing is sparse enough for that silence to register
motifs.rationale: Phrases breathe without being throttled: the held note and the rest give shape, while the sequence and the octave leap keep the line technically alive rather than merely tasteful.

motifs.rhythmSignature: Rolling arpeggio over a slow pulse with the bass note held across the whole bar
motifs.accentStructure: Only the lowest note of each arpeggio is accented; the rest are even, soft and unstressed
motifs.pitchContour: Descending inner voice against fixed ringing open strings, ending a step below where it began
motifs.spaceCharacter: Notes overlap and ring; nothing is damped and no rest is cut short
motifs.rationale: An inversion of the riff cell, slowed and opened out. Keeping fixed open strings under a falling inner voice produces the dark, unresolved colour the closing section needs.

gridAccents.purpose: Triplet-feel snare and tom fill placed inside the straight pulse, so the handover to the break has motion without changing the 4/4 feel

sections.tonalJob: Establishes the minor tonic over a pedal, with the flat second used only as passing colour
sections.motifTransformation: Stated plainly by one guitar and drums, with every rest left fully open
sections.entryIntent: Cold start on a downbeat hit, no count-in and no ramp
sections.exitIntent: Last bar leaves beat 4 empty so the break lands naked
sections.linkToNext: Same tempo and same cell; the break only tightens what is already running

gridAccents.purpose: Dense kick-and-snare fill that pushes into the bridge while the guitar holds a single accent, so the drums lead the transition

sections.tonalJob: Holds the tonic pedal; tension comes from rhythmic placement, not from new harmony
sections.motifTransformation: Cell compressed: the muted cluster doubles and the delayed beat-3 hit lands harder, while phrase length stays strictly four-square
sections.entryIntent: Full slam on beat 1 with the drums leading the attack
sections.exitIntent: Ends on a sustained accent and lets the room ring for one beat
sections.linkToPrevious: Direct continuation, no tempo and no metre change
sections.linkToNext: The bridge picks up the same cell but starts moving it instead of repeating it

gridAccents.purpose: Lead ornaments the final unresolved degree into the solo entry, keeping the straight groove intact underneath

sections.tonalJob: Lifts the pedal a fourth and then hangs on an unresolved degree instead of returning home
sections.motifTransformation: Break cell displaced an eighth and lifted a fourth; the lead doubles its accent points an octave up so it is recognisable yet clearly developed
sections.entryIntent: Guitar enters a half beat early over the break's ring-out
sections.exitIntent: Stops on an unresolved held note as the drums drop to a single crash
sections.linkToPrevious: Audibly the same cell, now moving and rising rather than repeating in place
sections.linkToNext: Hands the solo an unresolved pitch to start from

gridAccents.purpose: One bar of clearly articulated scale run rising into the second phrase; used once as a statement, not as a recurring device
Hammer-on and pull-off sequence kept on a single string with small intervals, so the line moves without a pick attack on every note
Wide-interval arpeggio through the tonic minor shape, register shifted up an octave to set up the peak note
Fill that lands the solo's last accent and begins easing the pulse toward the acoustic section

sections.tonalJob: Minor scale over the tonic pedal, reaching the flat sixth at the peak before settling onto the fifth
sections.motifTransformation: Motif stated, sequenced downward, then re-attacked an octave higher for the peak and released on a bent, vibrating note
sections.entryIntent: Lead enters alone on the bridge's unresolved pitch; backing joins on beat 2
sections.exitIntent: Final bent note sustains while the drums thin to a single ride pulse
sections.linkToPrevious: Takes the bridge's stored tension as its literal starting pitch
sections.linkToNext: The sustain decays straight into the acoustic entry; the pulse eases rather than drops

gridAccents.purpose: Rolling six-per-beat arpeggio that keeps the open strings ringing while the inner voice walks downward

sections.tonalJob: Same minor centre, now voiced with open strings so the tonic sits beneath moving inner notes
sections.motifTransformation: The riff cell inverted into a slow descending inner voice over fixed ringing open strings
sections.entryIntent: Enters underneath the solo's decaying sustain, with no gap and no count-in
sections.exitIntent: Settles onto the tonic with the upper voice still hanging a step above it
sections.linkToPrevious: Tempo eases by a small step, not a halving; the same subdivision is still felt
sections.linkToNext: The outro keeps the identical figure and simply thins it out

sections.tonalJob: Resolves to the tonic but keeps the second degree ringing, so it closes without brightening
sections.motifTransformation: Figure reduced to its skeleton; the second acoustic voice drops out for the final two bars
sections.entryIntent: Continues the same picking pattern with one voice removed and no new gesture
sections.exitIntent: Final chord left ringing until it decays on its own
sections.linkToPrevious: Identical figure, one small tempo step slower and thinner in texture

requestedTechniques.purpose: Establishes the muted low floor so the open accents and the rests are heard as events
Tight muted chug that makes the displaced beat-3 accent and the empty 'and' of 2 audible
Hard accents on the delayed hit while the kick keeps the true downbeat, so 4/4 is never lost
Short cut-offs around the migrating accent so the cell reads as developed rather than repeated
Lead doubles the rhythm accents an octave up to announce itself before the solo
Ascending legato inside one string, small intervals, so phrases move without a pick attack per note
Descending half of the sequence on the same string, keeping the run even and unbroken
Leaning half-step colour inside phrases, deliberately not used as the peak gesture
Whole-step bend onto the target note at the top of the phrase, the solo's main expressive move
Wide, hard vibrato on the sustained peak so it carries over the sparse backing
One wide upward slide into the register shift before the peak, used a single time so it reads as a slide and not as a bend
Rhythm guitar plays sparse stabs on beat 1 and the 'and' of 3 only, audible but never covering the lead
Open strings and bass notes held across bar lines so the harmony blurs and rings
Final chord left to decay naturally with nothing damped or cut

omittedRequests.reason: The output contract carries one articulation per note and has no cross-string sweep gesture, so it cannot be notated honestly. Rather than imitate it, the solo uses a genuine wide-interval arpeggio in bar 7, described as an arpeggio and nothing more.

You allowed bass to be skipped. Low-end weight is carried instead by the drop-tuned rhythm guitar and by a kick pattern written to answer the guitar accents, which keeps the arrangement inside the guitar-focused brief.

omittedRequests.request: Pinch harmonics and high squeals implied by the reference sound
omittedRequests.reason: They are not in the articulation set (accent, palm_mute, vibrato, bends, slide, legato, normal, sustain, staccato). Their bite is approximated with accent plus hard wide vibrato on peak notes; this is an approximation, not the technique itself.

omittedRequests.request: Flams and grace notes in the drum writing
omittedRequests.reason: Not expressible in this contract, which allows one articulation per note and no ornamental pre-strokes. Drum richness is instead produced by changing groove roles per section, kick-against-snare placement, and three differently shaped transition fills.
